taxonomy:
Below is a taxonomy for **grid-based logic/puzzle games**, organized by the *primary mechanism* (placement, coloring, drawing loops/paths, connectivity, partitioning, etc.). Each game from your list is placed into the most fitting category (some games could fit multiple categories, but each is assigned once for clarity).

---

## 1) Light / Visibility / Line-of-sight constraints
Games where illumination or visibility along rows/columns is central.

- **Akari** (light bulbs illuminate rows/columns; all white cells must be lit; no bulb sees another)
- **Kurodoko** (numbers count visible white cells until black cell/frame)
- **Kurotto** (numbers constrain contiguous black runs in row/column from circles)

---

## 2) Rectangle / Region partitioning (tiling) puzzles
Games where the board is partitioned into rectangles/regions/blocks with size/shape rules.

- **Chained Block** (blocks of black cells; chain of blocks by corner contact; unique shapes/sizes)
- **Double Choco** (partition into blocks; each block has matching white/gray shapes)
- **Five Cells** (partition into blocks of exactly 5 cells)
- **Fillomino** (partition into number-sized regions; same numbers fill blocks)
- **Hashiwokakero** (bridges connect islands; implicitly region-like connectivity, but core is graph)
- **Heyawake** (rooms by bold borders; painted cells constrained within rooms)
- **Nurimeizu** (rooms; each outlined region has two blocks of same size/number)
- **Nurimisaki** (rooms/maze-like walls; connectivity and size constraints)
- **Shikaku** (partition into rectangles; each rectangle has one number = area)
- **Shakashaka** (uncovered white cells form rectangles/squares; triangles placed)
- **Slitherlink** (loop on grid; not a partitioner—see Loop category)
- **Tilepaint** (tiles enclosed by bold lines; color tiles based on diagonal-number constraints)
- **Sto-stone** (rooms; number in room constrains continuous black cells)
- **Suraromu** (loop must pass gates; rooms not primary)
- **Usowan** (colored-cell placement with region constraints via bold rectangles)

---

## 3) Coloring / Black-White pattern puzzles (global constraints)
Games where the main action is coloring cells black/white with connectivity or adjacency rules.

- **Choco Banana** (paint some cells black; black forms rectangles; white cannot form rectangles)
- **Hitori** (black cells not touching; white cells connected; duplicates forbidden in rows/cols)
- **Heyawake** (painted cells cannot connect; white connectivity constraints)
- **Kurodoko** (black cells constrained; white connected)
- **LITS** (color tetrominoes; connectivity; no 2×2+ colored squares)
- **Nurikabe** (black wall connected; white regions each have one number)
- **Nuritwin** (shaded blocks in regions; two blocks per region; no touching; no 2×2 all shaded)
- **Nagareru** (loop with wind constraints—see Loop/Path category, but it’s not coloring)
- **Usowan** (colored cells cannot connect orthogonally; white not separated)
- **Yajilin** (black cells forbidden for loop; black cells cannot touch orthogonally)

---

## 4) Loop puzzles (single non-self-crossing loop)
Games where you draw one loop through cell centers/edges with turn/straight rules.

- **Dotchi-Loop** (loop through white circles; straight/turn consistency per enclosed area)
- **Masyu** (loop through circles; black/white circles impose turn/straight behavior)
- **Mid-loop** (loop passes through black circles; circle is midpoint of straight segment)
- **Moon-or-Sun** (loop visits each room once; moons/suns per room; alternation across rooms)
- **Nagareru** (single continuous loop with direction/wind constraints)
- **Suraromu** (single loop; must pass gates exactly once; start/end at open circle)
- **Yajilin** (single loop; avoids black cells and numbered cells; black cells not adjacent)
- **Slitherlink** (single loop through dots; numbers constrain surrounding edges)

---

## 5) Path / Line connection puzzles (non-loop)
Games where you draw paths/lines connecting endpoints or forming routes, not necessarily a closed loop.

- **Hashiwokakero** (bridges connect islands; graph connectivity)
- **Hebi** (numbered snake segments 1→5; directional/visibility constraints)
- **Numberlink** (connect pairs with continuous lines; no crossing/branching)
- **Pencils** (draw pencil lines from tips; length constraints)
- **Ripple Effect** (fill rooms with consecutive numbers; spacing constraints—more like numeric placement, but it’s route-like)
- **Satogaeri** (move circles through grid tracks; each country has one circle; movement constraints)
- **Yosenabe** (move circles into gray areas; arrows show straight movement; sum constraints)

---

## 6) Snake / sequential-entity puzzles
Games explicitly about snakes/ordered sequences.

- **Hebi** (snake with head/tail numbers; snakes cannot touch; directional attack rule)
- **Nagareru** (wind-blown loop is not a snake, but it’s directional movement; still loop category)
- **Norinori** (blocks placed in pairs in consecutive black squares—more like placement/tiling)

---

## 7) Placement of polyominoes / shapes
Games where you place fixed-shape pieces or shape-constrained blocks.

- **Evolomino** (place squares on arrows; blocks grow by adding one square without rotation/flip)
- **LITS** (tetrominoes in bold areas; rotated/reversed tetrominoes cannot touch except corners)
- **Sashigane** (L-shaped blocks; open circles mark knee; arrows point to knee)
- **Chained Block** (blocks of black cells with unique shapes in a chain)

---

## 8) Arithmetic / numeric grid-filling (Sudoku-like or number-driven placement)
Games where numbers are placed/filled with arithmetic or strict numeric constraints.

- **Sudoku** (standard 1–9 rows/cols/3×3 blocks)
- **Nansuke** (fill blanks with digits from a list; row/column orientation)
- **Ripple Effect** (rooms contain consecutive numbers; spacing between duplicates)
- **Fillomino** (numbers define region sizes; also region partitioning)
- **Kurodoko / Kurotto / Akari** (numbers constrain counts/visibility; also visibility category)

---

## 9) Arrow / direction / movement constraint puzzles
Games where arrows or directed movement are key.

- **Nagareru** (wind direction from arrows; loop cannot advance against wind)
- **Pencils** (pencil tip direction; line passes through cells)
- **Satogaeri** (circles move vertically/horizontally; track-crossing restrictions)
- **Yajilin** (arrows indicate direction for counting black cells)
- **Yosenabe** (arrows show movement of circles into gray areas)

---
